document.title: Low Vision PDF — Reflow PDFs for low-vision reading

welcomeDialog.heading: Welcome to Low Vision PDF
welcomeDialog.description: This tool helps you prepare a PDF for easier low-vision reading. All processing happens in your browser—nothing is uploaded to a server. After optional text extraction to verify the document, choose Automatic splitting to slice each page into larger strips, or Manual cropping to draw boxes on each page yourself (you can add any number of regions per page). Then generate the reflowed view and print, or download a new PDF. Manual downloads place each segment on a US Letter page with margins so printing fits predictably.
welcomeDialog.bullet1: Upload your PDF and check the first-page preview.
welcomeDialog.bullet2: Optional: extract text to verify the document (including OCR for scanned pages).
welcomeDialog.bullet3: Configure layout: Automatic splitting uses segments, direction, rotation, and optional margin trimming; Manual cropping defines regions separately on every page.
welcomeDialog.bullet4: Generate the reflowed view, then use Download reflowed PDF or your browser’s Print dialog.

header.tagline: Reflow PDF pages into large, split segments for low-vision reading. All processing stays in your browser.

step1.heading: Step 1: Upload
step1.description: Select a single PDF. Nothing is uploaded to a server.
step1.previewAriaLabel: Preview of the first page of the selected PDF

step2.heading: Step 2: Verify (text extraction)
step2.description: Embedded text is read with the same PDF engine used for rendering. If the PDF has no embedded text (for example a scan), Tesseract runs in your browser (WASM) to OCR each page—nothing is uploaded. Use this after upload to confirm you have the correct document before you adjust layout options.
step2.textareaAriaLabel: Plain text extracted from the PDF for verification
step2.placeholder: Text will appear here after extraction.

step3.heading: Step 3: Configuration
step3.alertManual: Manual cropping requires drawing regions on the screen and requires sight. If you are using a screen reader, please use Automatic splitting.
step3.noRegionsDefined: Open “Define crop regions” and draw one or more boxes on each page as needed.
step3.autoContrastDesc: Stretches brightness on each page to help faded or low-contrast scans.
step3.autoDeskewDesc: Straightens pages that were scanned slightly crooked (typical small skew only).
step3.trimMarginsDesc: Crops each page to the bounding box of visible ink before splitting.
step3.smartCropDesc: When splitting automatically, adjusts cut lines to gaps between text and images so blocks are not cut in half.
step3.undoAriaLabel: Undo margin trimming and regenerate output using full pages

step4.heading: Step 4: Process, view, and download
step4.description: Workers render and split the PDF off the main thread. Large files may take a moment.
step4.saveDesc: Saves one PDF page per segment image, sized to match each image, for printing or sharing. Your browser’s Print dialog is still available if you prefer.

footer.description: Low Vision PDF — client-side only. After generating the reflowed view, use Download reflowed PDF or your browser’s print dialog to print or save as PDF.

cropModal.heading: Define Crop Regions
cropModal.instructionBasic: Choose a page, then click and drag on the image to draw boxes. You can add any number of regions per page. Repeat for each page.
cropModal.pageAriaLabel: Which PDF page to define crops for
